note: MDC area of wooded hills and small fishing lakes north of Silex. Two primitive camping areas, each with a privy and no pads, tables or water: one off County Road 226 on the west side, a small gravel lot and turnaround in the woods south of Lake 4; the other on Robey Road south of Route RA, a gravel loop about 50 m across around a grass island, across the road from the Lake 7 lot. Neither sees its lake. Open fires only in designated areas. Area gates are closed from October 1 through the end of spring turkey season, which may shut interior roads. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: two designated primitive camping areas (map symbols + GIS points), each with a privy. The pinned west one is a small lot; the east one on Robey Road is a built gravel loop 2.75 km away - split candidate / better pin, owner's call. The page's bare 'Camping is prohibited.' is the known artifact. Free/FCFS/14 nights/no hookups confirmed. Not waterfront stands. Phone matches.
flags: 'CAMPING IS PROHIBITED.' - PAGE ARTIFACT: the page prints the bare line 'Camping is prohibited.' directly after the standard Rule 140 paragraphs, while 'Things To Do' lists Camping - 'Individual Campsites'. Brochure: 'Campers are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period in designated areas.' The 05/14 map legend has 'Primitive Camping Area' and draws two; GIS layer 27 has both. Read as the artifact the brief describes; camping is allowed.

TWO CAMPING AREAS, WHAT IS ON THE GROUND: (1) WEST, the stored pin 39.15142,-91.05136: where County Road 226 enters the area by Lake 4 - a gravel lot about 10 x 30 m with the GIS point on it, and 45 m east a small gravel turnaround loop about 25 m across with vehicles parked on it; map Privy symbol beside it. A designated point at a lot - stays. (2) EAST, 39.14297,-91.02142: on the west side of Robey Road 600 m south of Route RA - a gravel loop about 50 m across around a mown grass island with shade trees, entered from Robey Road, clearly a made camping loop; the Lake 7 parking lot is 40 m across the road; map Privy symbol beside it. The east one is the better camp: built loop, larger, 600 m of gravel from the paved route.

SPLIT CANDIDATE / PIN, OWNER'S CALL: the two are 2.75 km apart in a straight line, on different roads with their own entrances (CR 226 from Route UU on the west; Robey Road from Route RA on the east), and the east one is a loop rather than a single lot, so the split rule's test is met for it. Nothing else in the database within 3 km of either. If the owner prefers one entry, the pin would be better moved to the east loop, 39.14297,-91.02142 (old 39.15142,-91.05136); the note describes both either way.

GATES: brochure: 'Area gates are closed from October 1 through the end of spring turkey season.' It does not say which gates. The east loop opens straight off Robey Road, a through county road, and the west lot is at the end of County Road 226, so neither obviously sits behind an area gate, but that is not confirmed by any page - worded as a caution in the note. No dated closure notice on the page.
FIRES: brochure 'No open fires except in designated areas.' - in the note.
HORSE CAMP: none. Brochure: 'Horseback riding is allowed on roads open to' vehicles; no horse camp marked. A shooting range is at the centre of the area, 1.3 km from either camp.
PRIVIES: the map draws a Privy symbol beside each camping symbol; vault_toilets written from the map.

WATERFRONT - NOT WATERFRONT STANDS: west - Lake 4 (a few acres) is 80-90 m north through closed woods; east - Lake 7 is about 110 m north-east beyond the road, the lot and trees. Both lakes are pond-sized and unseen from the camps.
PHONE: stored 636-441-4554 matches the page's 'For more information call (636) 441-4554'.
